title: The quiet case for slower cities
dek: We design streets to move people quickly. Perhaps the better question is how long they want to stay.
body: Every city plan I have read in the past decade promises to shave minutes off journeys. Few promise to make the minutes themselves better.
The places people love most, the old shophouse rows and the void decks where neighbours linger, are not efficient. They are generous.
A slower city is not a less ambitious one. It is one that measures success by how people feel when they arrive, not how quickly they leave.
caption: A shophouse street lined with small businesses.

title: ASEAN’s next decade will be decided at sea
dek: Ports, cables and fishing grounds matter more to the region’s future than any summit communiqué.
body: Most of Southeast Asia’s trade, data and protein crosses water. Yet regional diplomacy still treats the sea as a backdrop rather than the stage.
The countries that invest in shared maritime rules now will set the terms of the region’s economy for a generation.
That means joint patrols, common standards for cable protection and a fisheries agreement with real enforcement.
caption: Fishing boats moored in open water.

title: We should teach children to argue well, not just to answer well
dek: Exam systems reward the right answer. Life rewards the person who can change their mind in public.
body: Our schools are superb at producing students who can find the right answer. They are less good at producing adults who can disagree without falling out.
Structured debate, taught early and often, is one of the cheapest ways to change that.
The goal is not to win arguments but to understand the strongest version of the other side.
caption: Students follow a teacher’s presentation.

title: Our parents need tech help too, not just our children
dek: We worry about screen time for kids. We should worry just as much about elders left behind by every new app.
body: Every month, another everyday task moves into an app: booking a clinic visit, paying a bill, ordering a meal.
For many older people, each change is a small wall. Most will not complain. They will simply stop doing the thing.
Patient, in-person help at community centres works. It deserves the same attention and funding we give to children’s digital lessons.
caption: An older woman smiles at a message on her phone.
